question.problem:
Rationalize the denominator of the following expression:

| ${p}^{2}\sqrt{36}$ | __ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $2\sqrt{3s}$ | __ | $s$ |
question.worked_solution:
We must remove the radical $\sqrt{3s}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{3s},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{p}^{2}\sqrt{36}}{2\sqrt{3s}} & = \\ \frac{{p}^{2}\sqrt{36}}{2\sqrt{3s}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3s}}{\sqrt{3s}} & = \\ \frac{6{p}^{2}\cdot \sqrt{3s}}{2\sqrt{3s}\cdot \sqrt{3s}} & = \\ \frac{6{p}^{2}\sqrt{3s}}{2{(\sqrt{3s})}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{6{p}^{2}\sqrt{3s}}{2\cdot 3s} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{6}{p}^{2}\sqrt{3s}}{\cancel{6}s} & = \\ \frac{{p}^{2}\sqrt{3s}}{s}\end{aligned}
$$
